Why Tencent Bears Were Right Before The Drop
sum: Tencent has spent the past year in the headlines for AI, cloud expansion, and fresh regulatory twists, from Nvidia chip approvals that stalled in Beijing to a multibillion dollar Oracle chip leasing deal that never actually went ahead. Investors who held Tencent over the past year are down 32.4%, including dividends. If that outcome sat on your own portfolio statement, how confident would you feel that the heavy AI spend and global push are still worth backing?
The move put Tencent in the middle of this trade. Scan 53 AI infrastructure stocks for other companies exposed to it.
The shares cost HK$629 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Tencent then had to choose which earnings story felt more realistic.

On the optimistic side, analysts argued the stock was worth about HK$687 as a fair value anchor, based on assumptions that revenue could compound at 10.5% with profit margins reaching 31.6% and a future P/E of 23.0x over three years.

The more cautious case put fair value nearer HK$508, with expectations of 12.0% annual revenue growth but profit margins capped at 24.0% and a future P/E of 22.0x over a longer five year horizon, while regulatory risk stayed front and center.

Tencent’s heavy AI push showed up clearly in the Q2 2026 numbers. Revenue moved to CNY 204.8b and net income edged to CNY 56.0b, yet the net margin slipped from 30.2% to 27.4%. That combination supported the cautious case that higher AI spending and chip constraints would weigh on profitability even as the top line held up.
The lesson is simple. When a story hinges on AI investment lifting future earnings, keep an eye on the net margin line and how it moves against any revenue increase, not just the headline growth.

items.t: Hong Kong Stocks Surge 877 Points to Breach 24,000 Mark; Turnover Hits HK$356.6 Billion, a Near Four-Month High
sum: Hong Kong stocks on the 5th bucked the trend seen in other major Asian markets. The Hang Seng Index closed sharply higher by 877 points, or 3.67%, at 24,796, reclaiming the 24,000-point threshold in one stroke. Full-day turnover reached HK$356.6 billion (approximately $45.5 billion), marking the largest single-day volume in nearly four months. On the same day, Japanese and Taiwanese stocks both fell more than 2%, making Hong Kong's contrarian strength the most conspicuous focus in the region.

Across the board, aside from artificial intelligence (AI)-related names, nearly all sectors advanced, with traditional tech platform stocks in online shopping, gaming, and retail posting particularly strong gains. Tencent Holdings (0700.HK) closed at HK$430 (approximately $55), up 7.17%; Alibaba (9988.HK) closed at HK$109 (approximately $14), up 8.44%; and Meituan (3690.HK) closed at HK$80.3 (approximately $10), up 6.78%. The Hang Seng Tech Index opened higher in the morning session at 3,992.39, up 56.37 points, or 1.43%.

The capital driving this rally came from multiple directions. Market participants noted that after the US midterm election results became clear, some funds withdrew from US AI stocks and rotated into Hong Kong equities. Stabilizing international geopolitical conditions and falling oil prices also eased market pressure. In addition, the People's Bank of China's stated support for measures such as share buybacks gave the market room to imagine capital inflows into Hong Kong stocks.

On the corporate front, Tencent's long-teased next-generation large language model, the official version of Hunyuan Hy4, was released on the 4th. The series' parameter scale rose from under 300B in Hy3 to 770B, with the next generation, Hy5, set to expand further. Hy4 also introduced visual understanding capabilities for the first time and supports computer operation. This development became an important catalyst for Tencent's share price. Other internet and tech stocks strengthened in tandem: Xiaomi rose more than 4%, while Meituan and NetEase gained more than 3%. Gold stocks opened higher, with Zijin Gold International up more than 7%. Innovative drug concept stocks extended their gains, with BeiGene up more than 2%.

Oracle Stock Slips After $7 Billion Tencent Deal Is Canceled
sum: Oracle Corporation ORCL has canceled a $7 billion chip leasing deal with Tencent after U.S. officials raised concerns with the company, the Financial Times reported, citing two people familiar with the matter. Oracle shares were down 2.30% in premarket.

The agreement would have leased 100,000 chips to Tencent in the Chinese firm's largest ever overseas deal. The cancellation follows another FT report on Tuesday that Nvidia Corporation NVDA has told its cloud partners to sell at least 51% of their services to non-Chinese companies. Many Chinese firms have relied on leasing computing capacity through overseas cloud arrangements for AI work.
The report lands two days after Oracle filed to raise $20 billion through a note sale and a concurrent stock offering.

Why Tencent Music Bears Were Right Before A 61% Drop
sum: If you had bought Tencent Music Entertainment Group at the start of this review period expecting smartphone adoption, fan clubs and live shows to re-rate the business, the result has been brutal. Investors who held Tencent Music Entertainment Group over the past year are down 60.5%, including dividends. If that entry decision was based on analysts’ 2025 assumptions for double digit revenue growth, still high margins and a near 30x future P/E, what exactly did that thesis overlook?
The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.
The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing Up On Tencent Music Entertainment Group
The shares cost US$22.31 at the start of the period, and Tencent Music Entertainment Group sat between two very different stories about what came next.

On the upbeat side, one narrative put Fair Value at US$28.34. That view leaned on 14.8% assumed annual revenue growth, helped by rising smartphone usage, fan-focused features such as SVIP and "bubble," and a 29.8x future P/E assumption.

The more cautious script pointed to a Fair Value of US$14.54. This camp focused on tightening Chinese regulation, higher compliance costs, and fierce competition from platforms like NetEase Cloud Music and ByteDance as key risks to future performance.

The big swing factor was Tencent Music Entertainment Group closing the US$2.4b Himalaya acquisition and folding podcast revenue into Q2 2026, which helped lift total revenue to RMB 8,933m and supported the optimistic case on new formats and fan time spent. At the same time, net margin slipped from 28.5% to 27.7%, which challenged the easy high margin assumption.

sum: US indexes dipped as AI and semiconductor stocks sold off after major technology companies reported disappointing earnings, amid broader concerns about AI spending and profitability.

Concern over the AI trade remains the dominant cross-market theme, after disappointing technology earnings intensified Friday’s US selloff, stockbroking and portfolio management subsidiary of First National Bank (FNB) said in a brief on Monday.

According to market reports, the NASDAQ ended 2.86% lower last week, while the S&P 500 lost 1.82% and the Dow Jones fell 1.09%. Market analysts said US futures are firmer ahead of major earnings, the jobs report, ISM surveys, and the mid-term elections.
Europe proved more resilient despite sovereign debt sustainability concerns, with the FTSE 100 ending the week up 0.07%, while the Euro Stoxx 50 declined 1.22%.
In Asia on Monday, technology shares are supporting Hong Kong, where the Hang Seng Index is trading 0.61% higher, although weak Chinese PMI readings and AI valuation concerns are tempering sentiment.

The Nikkei 225 is up 0.44%. Australia’s ASX 200 closed down 0.58%, as weakness in technology, mining and healthcare outweighed stronger banks ahead of Tuesday’s expected Reserve Bank of Australia rate increase.

In South Africa, the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) is set for a firmer open this morning, with positive global futures and a broad recovery across most Asian markets setting the stage for a rebound after the All Share and Top 40 closed lower.

Tencent stock: Q3 results set for November 18 as AI spending weighs
sum: Tencent is scheduled to publish its third-quarter 2026 results on Wednesday, November 18. The company's investor relations page lists the release in its 2026 calendar, while Futu's Oct. 15 earnings preview provides the market context.

Futu reported that GF Securities expects Tencent's third-quarter revenue to reach RMB 209.8 billion, an increase of 9 percent from a year earlier. UBS expects revenue growth of 7 percent. The forecasts point to continued expansion, but they also frame the quarter around the cost of Tencent's artificial intelligence build-out.

Futu said UBS estimates AI-related operating expenses at RMB 16 billion for the quarter and adjusted operating profit at RMB 71 billion, down 2 percent year over year. GF Securities expects adjusted operating profit of RMB 70 billion, a 4 percent decline. The figures suggest that infrastructure depreciation and research spending could absorb part of the benefit from higher-margin activities.

Advertising is expected to remain a major growth driver, with the two research houses cited by Futu forecasting an 18 percent year-over-year increase. Domestic gaming revenue is forecast to grow by 12 to 13 percent, while overseas gaming revenue is expected to decline by 3 to 6 percent as Supercell faces a high comparison base and a limited new-title pipeline.

Futu also reported that UBS raised its Tencent target price by 3.9 percent to HKD 740, while GF Securities set a fair target price of HKD 644.54. These analyst estimates remain forward-looking and will be tested by the official results next week.
Tencent stock traded at 43.89 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:18 CET on Sunday, November 1, 2026.

sum: Xiaomi shares came back to life on Thursday after a difficult run, jumping more than 7% in Hong Kong as investors returned to technology names and looked again at the company’s fast-growing electric-vehicle business.

That is a strong one-day move, but it needs some context. Xiaomi stock remains well below the highs it reached over the past year, and investors are still trying to decide how much value to place on the company’s EV ambitions while its traditional smartphone business deals with tougher margins.
Thursday’s rally suggests the market has not lost interest in the growth story.
Hong Kong’s technology shares were broadly stronger as long-term US bond yields eased and investors became slightly more willing to take risk again.
The Hang Seng Tech Index moved higher, while Alibaba, Tencent, Meituan and other major technology stocks also gained.
At one point it was up more than 5% while several peers were posting increases of closer to 1% or 2%. The stock later extended the gain above 7%.
That suggests the wider Hong Kong tech rally helped, but it was probably not the entire explanation.

sum: Tencent Holdings (TCEHY) shares rose more than 5% in Hong Kong on Tuesday after the company introduced a new image-generation system, adding another step to its push into consumer artificial intelligence.

The Hy Image 3.5 Preview model is being added to Tencent's Yuanbao chatbot as well as tools used for video editing and design. The company said the system improves on its previous version and expands its AI capabilities beyond text.

Tencent is also positioning the technology for its broader WeChat ecosystem, which serves more than one billion users. The company has been increasing its focus on practical AI applications as competition intensifies among Chinese technology companies.

The launch coincided with Alibaba Group (BABA) holding its annual AI conference, where it outlined plans for much larger AI models and introduced a new chip. The developments highlight the growing competition among Chinese technology companies as they build domestic AI capabilities.

Tencent's latest model was tested internally by hundreds of designers. The company said the system performed around the level of ByteDance's Seedream 5.0 Pro in those tests, while comparisons with competing models showed varying results.

Meta's AI Assistant Muse Goes Viral; Tencent Surges 5% as Hang Seng Index Rises for Third Straight Day, Up 45 Points
sum: Meta Platforms' personal AI assistant app Muse has rapidly gained traction in the U.S. market, topping Apple's App Store free app chart less than two weeks after launch. The AI agent frenzy drove overnight gains in U.S. chip stocks, with the Nasdaq Composite surging 2.26% to a record closing high of 27,122 points. The bullish sentiment spilled over into Asian markets, with Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index closing higher for a third consecutive session on the 22nd, finishing at 25,087 points, up 45 points or 0.18%, on main-board turnover of HK$249.214 billion (approximately $31.8 billion).

The Hang Seng Tech Index rose 14 points or 0.34% to close at 4,438 points, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index gained 22 points or 0.28% to end at 8,362 points. The broader market climbed more than 200 points in early trading, but gains narrowed significantly in the afternoon, reflecting investor caution ahead of the meeting between U.S. President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Xi is expected to visit the United States from the 23rd to the 25th, and hopes for improved U.S.-China relations supported early sentiment, though uncertainty over the outcome of the talks limited further upside.

Muse has captured intense market attention because it allows users to create customized AI agents that can read content from their Facebook and Instagram accounts and connect to third-party applications. This signals that AI agents are moving from enterprise applications into the mass consumer market, with a path toward commercial monetization becoming increasingly clear. The market is betting this will drive broad-based demand for inference computing, server CPUs, memory, and optical communications infrastructure.

Tencent (00700.HK) emerged as the biggest beneficiary of this AI agent wave, closing up 5.02% at HK$458.4 (approximately $58), its highest level since mid-August and the best-performing blue-chip constituent. Markets are focused on Tencent's native AI agent "Xiaowei" within the WeChat ecosystem, with expectations that it could rival Meta's Muse by leveraging WeChat's massive user base to develop similar consumer-grade application scenarios.

Netmarble’s Bang to buy 13.4% stake from Tencent affiliate for $270mn
sum: Bang Jun-hyuk, chairman of Netmarble Corp. and Coway Co., will acquire a 13.4 percent stake in Netmarble held by a Tencent Holdings Ltd. affiliate for 374 billion won ($270 million).

Netmarble said in a regulatory filing Friday that Bang will buy a 13.41 percent stake from Han River Investment Pte., which currently holds an 18.11 percent stake in Netmarble. The transaction is valued at 374 billion won.
The transaction is scheduled to close on September 21 through an after-hours block trade, at 33,538 won per share.
The deal comes as Tencent moves to sell part of its stake in Netmarble.

Netmarble said the deal is intended to strengthen “responsible management,” explaining that Bang, the company’s largest shareholder, will directly acquire the stake to actively reduce uncertainty that could arise if a large block of shares were released onto the market.
Following the transaction, Bang’s stake in Netmarble will rise from 24.93 percent to 38.34 percent, while Han River Investment’s holding will fall to 4.69 percent.
Netmarble said its business cooperation with Tencent will continue without disruption despite the change in Tencent’s ownership stake.

Netmarble Chairman Bang Jun-hyuk to buy company shares from Tencent affiliate
sum: Bang Jun-hyuk, chairman of South Korean game developer Netmarble, will acquire most of the company’s share package held by Han River Investment, an entity affiliated with Tencent. The transaction is expected to be worth 374 billion won, or about $270 million. This is reported by Korea Herald.

Han River Investment planned to sell part of its 18.1% stake in Netmarble. Bang Jun-hyuk agreed to purchase 11.15 million shares at a price of 33,538 won per share. The transaction is scheduled to close on September 21.

Netmarble stated that the agreed price includes a discount for a block transaction compared with the company’s average share price during the month before negotiations began. As the deal is concluded between shareholders, Netmarble itself will not receive funds from the sale.

After the transaction is completed, Bang Jun-hyuk’s stake in Netmarble will increase from 24.93% to 38.34%. At the same time, Han River Investment’s stake will decrease to 4.69%. The gap between the stakes of the two largest shareholders will increase from 6.82 to 33.65 percentage points.

In a regulatory filing, Netmarble named the strengthening of responsible management as the purpose of the acquisition. Han River Investment explained the sale by the need to recover investment funds. According to the publication, Bang Jun-hyuk is expected to finance the purchase with a loan secured by shares; details of the collateral and other terms are to be disclosed later.

Netmarble also noted that the change in ownership structure will not affect its cooperation with Tencent. The companies have worked together since 2014, when Tencent invested 530 billion won in CJ Games, Netmarble’s predecessor.

Chinese tech giant Tencent sees spending surge, defends potential 'superior' AI returns
sum: Tencent on Wednesday posted a surge in spending in the second quarter, with executives touting the potential of "superior" returns on the company's investment in China's cut-throat AI market.

The company said capital expenditures for the June quarter rose 65% to 52.8 billion yuan ($7.8 billion) from the previous quarter, as it continues to ramp up buying and building computing infrastructure to monetize its AI models. The company said its free cash flow came in at negative 13.8 billion yuan in the quarter.

"At the infrastructure level, we substantially stepped up our procurement of compute, which will enable us to convert usage of our applications and models into revenue going forward," Tencent CEO Ma Huateng said in a statement accompanying the earnings release.

During the earnings call, most of the questions asked by analysts related to the potential return on Tencent's capex: a theme across this tech earnings season in the U.S. that is filtering through to China.

In response to one analyst's question, Chief Strategy Officer James Mitchell said the company could achieve a "decent return in an immediate timeframe" if the tech giant rented out all of its compute capacity.

Instead, Tencent is using some of the capacity to build "state-of-the-art" AI models and applications of its own, which Mitchell said would translate to "superior economic returns over the longer term."

Tencent also said on the earnings call that its cloud business grew at a rate of a "low-twenties" percentage thanks to AI demand and international expansion. The company said it was able to raise prices for Tencent Cloud customers.

Sharp decline in Tencent stock leads sell-off of Chinese video game shares
sum: Tencent's Hong Kong-listed shares fell more than 7% in Wednesday trading, its biggest daily drop since April 2025, amid a sell-off of Chinese video-game stocks on concerns over a decline...

The Hang Seng Tech Index fell 3.5%, dragged down by stocks such as NetEase and XD, which dropped more than 6%. BNP Paribas told clients that the sell-off came after rumors spread about a decline in Tencent's revenue from games on smart devices.

The decline comes after a strong rally in previous weeks, with the stock rising about 10% in the first three weeks of July, prompting some investors to take profits ahead of the second-quarter results announcement on August 12.

Market estimates suggest the company could post total game revenue growth of 11% in the fiscal quarter ended June, according to Bloomberg data, despite declining game revenue both domestically and internationally in the first quarter.

Analysts believe that Hong Kong-listed stocks remain more vulnerable to capital flows than their mainland counterparts due to the lack of government support. The rumors about Tencent's revenue combined with investment funds' moves toward AI stocks fueled the sell-off in the gaming sector.
Portfolio managers point to the declining importance of the gaming sector in driving Tencent's growth, although it remains one of the company's main revenue sources.

Tencent inks first deal for carbon-removal credits outside China
sum: [BEIJING] Tencent Holdings will buy 300,000 carbon removal credits from an agroforestry project in Indonesia, marking the first deal of its kind for the Chinese technology firm outside its domestic market.

Tencent has entered a 10-year agreement with Singapore-based carbon developer Thryve.Earth to purchase credits generated from a project on the island of Sulawesi, it said on Wednesday (Jul 8). Alphabet’s Google struck a separate 10-year offtake deal for 260,000 credits from the same project, while consulting firm McKinsey agreed to buy 75,000. The average price for agroforestry credits in Asia is currently around US$21.40, according to carbon data company Sylvera.

Carbon removal will play a key role in Tencent’s commitment to achieve carbon neutrality in its own operations and supply chain by 2030, a company spokesperson said by email. While reducing emissions remains the top priority, high-quality carbon credits can help address residual emissions and deliver climate impacts, the spokesperson said.

Agroforestry projects, which combine agriculture with removing carbon by planting or increasing forest cover, have the potential to deliver up to 310 million tons of carbon-dioxide removal annually and could play an important role in efforts to limit global warming. The willingness of corporate buyers to keep doing such deals offers a counterpoint to news earlier this year that Microsoft Corp was pulling back.

The Thryve.Earth project will restore degraded land in Sulawesi, an island in the centre of the Indonesian archipelago on which tropical rainforests have been destroyed by agriculture, soil erosion and invasive species. The idea is to develop a “mixed crop farming system” that sequesters carbon, replenishes soils, increases biodiversity and provides income for local farmers.

The project envisages an upper tree canopy of sugar palm plants and timber trees, a mid-layer of papayas, avocado, coffee, and bananas, and ground-level annual crops such as chilli and corn. The layers are intended to optimise land productivity and provide income streams that are “significantly more valuable than the carbon revenues alone, aligning carbon sequestration benefits with economic incentives,” Thryve.Earth said.

Kuaishou shares tumble as Tencent slashes stake after US$3b Kling AI deal
sum: The divestment will reduce Tencent’s shareholding in Kuaishou to 9.37 per cent from 15.68 per cent

Shares of Kuaishou Technology plunged 12 per cent on Tuesday after Tencent Holdings slashed its stake in the short-video platform by selling 273 million Class B shares, just days after leading a US$3 billion financing round for Kuaishou’s artificial intelligence video unit, Kling AI.
The filing did not disclose the transaction price or range, but based on Kuaishou’s closing price of HK$46 on Monday, Tencent is expected to raise HK$12.56 billion (US$1.6 billion) from the sale.

Hong Kong Stocks Extend Rebound: Tencent, Meituan Surge Nearly 5%; Nvidia Kyber Delay Rumors Spark PCB Stock Bloodbath
sum: Hong Kong stocks extended their rebound momentum on Monday, with the Hang Seng Index closing firmly above the 23,600-point level, lifted by heavyweight tech stocks and the innovative drug sector. However, the session was rocked by reports of delays to Nvidia's next-generation architecture, triggering a supply chain shock that sent PCB (printed circuit board) and semiconductor concept stocks tumbling in a sharply polarized market.

At the close, the Hang Seng Index rose 1.14% to 23,616.32 points; the Hang Seng Tech Index added 0.94% to 4,541.23 points; and the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index led gains, surging 1.46% to 7,812.35 points. Market activity was robust, with total daily turnover reaching HK$314.72 billion (approximately $40.1 billion).

Fund flows also provided positive signals, as southbound capital poured in with net purchases totaling HK$20.53 billion (approximately $2.6 billion) for the day. Of this, the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect recorded net purchases of HK$12.55 billion (approximately $1.6 billion), while the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect saw net purchases of HK$7.97 billion (approximately $1.0 billion), indicating that mainland Chinese investor confidence in the Hong Kong market is gradually recovering.

Heavyweight technology stocks formed the core pillar supporting the broader market. Kuaishou (01024.HK) led gains, surging nearly 8%. Market sources indicated that Morgan Stanley views its core business valuation multiples as highly attractive, and the company's recent restructuring of AI assets has sparked expectations of a valuation re-rating. Tencent Holdings (00700.HK) and Meituan (03690.HK) also performed strongly, rising approximately 4.8% and 4.7% respectively; Alibaba (09988.HK) also gained nearly 2%.

Tencent-related concept stocks generally moved higher. Maoyan Entertainment (01896.HK) jumped over 8%, while Tongcheng Travel (00780.HK) and ZhongAn Online P&C Insurance (06060.HK) followed suit. Market reports noted that Tencent's office AI agent, WorkBuddy, has recently gone viral, surpassing 20 million monthly active users and 13 million daily active users, with user stickiness approaching that of overseas collaboration software Slack, injecting a strong dose of confidence into the related ecosystem.
